title.value: Plan weekly family logistics around schedules and custody

introduction.value: A parent built a Claude Code skill that takes schedules, dietary profiles, cooking ability and the custody calendar to coordinate who is home, cooking and picking up kids.

method.value: The parent put their family’s schedules, dietary profiles, cooking ability, and 50/50 custody calendar into a single Claude Code SKILL.md file, then connected Claude to Google Calendar, Gmail, Notion, and Chrome via MCP. Claude used that context to generate a Sunday-night weekly briefing, assign realistic meals based on who was home and able to cook, draft co-parent logistics emails, and scan grocery prices across stores before loading carts through Chrome MCP.

outcome.value: They say the cooking-assignment logic became the most useful part because it matched meals to the parent actually available that night. Their first grocery test projected about $4.3K a year in savings, and they also say splitting a 40-item list across four stores beat a single store by 30–40%, though a commenter questioned whether those savings were inflated.

notes.value: It was built as just a markdown skill file with no app, backend, or database, but the author says MCP setup can be finicky.

source_text.body:
Plan weekly family logistics around schedules and custody
A parent built a Claude Code skill that takes schedules, dietary profiles, cooking ability and the custody calendar to coordinate who is home, cooking and picking up kids.
Done with
CC
Claude Code
What they did
The parent put their family’s schedules, dietary profiles, cooking ability, and 50/50 custody calendar into a single Claude Code SKILL.md file, then connected Claude to Google Calendar, Gmail, Notion, and Chrome via MCP. Claude used that context to generate a Sunday-night weekly briefing, assign realistic meals based on who was home and able to cook, draft co-parent logistics emails, and scan grocery prices across stores before loading carts through Chrome MCP.
How it went
They say the cooking-assignment logic became the most useful part because it matched meals to the parent actually available that night. Their first grocery test projected about $4.3K a year in savings, and they also say splitting a 40-item list across four stores beat a single store by 30–40%, though a commenter questioned whether those savings were inflated.
Worth knowing
It was built as just a markdown skill file with no app, backend, or database, but the author says MCP setup can be finicky.
Try it yourself
with
Claude Code
Copy prompt
I want a reusable weekly family planner. Read the files in [folder with schedules, custody calendar, dietary notes, and who can cook what], then build a skill that each week produces a day-by-day plan showing who is home, who cooks what dinner, and who handles each pickup. Respect [dietary restrictions] and flag any day where nobody is available for pickup. You're done when you've saved a one-page plan for [coming week] and shown it to me before anything is shared.
Original source: https://www.reddit.com/r/ClaudeAI/comments/1rs75si/i_built_an_opensource_claude_code_skill_to_run
